reasoning: Hero is BTN IP-closing with AdKd on QhJc9d, facing a 2.5bb (~26% pot) c-bet from MP-opener with CO sandwiched as middle caller-or-folder. Hero holds the nut gutshot (any T = AKQJT broadway), two clean overcards subject to dirtying against QJ9-heavy continuing ranges, and the Ad as a meaningful blocker to AQ/AJ/AA combos and to backdoor diamond runouts. No made pair, no current FD (single diamond on board, BDFD only). Pot odds 2.5 into 12 = 20.8%; required equity threshold is comfortably exceeded by the gutshot alone (~16% direct + ~5% BDFD + ~6-8% overcard equity, even discounted MW). MP's 26%-pot range-bet on QJ9 is structurally wide — this is a board where MP's preflop opening range smashes hard (KQ, KT, QQ, JJ, 99, TT, AQ, KJ, T9s, QJs, KJs, AK, AJs all continue with significant equity), so small-sizing keeps in floats and gives up little fold equity. Crucially CO is still live; CO flatted UTG-style preflop with a capped range (no AK/AA/KK; mostly 88-TT, suited broadway, suited connectors, QJs/JTs/T9s) that hits this board hard. Sandwiching IS the dominant feature here: a raise to ~10-11bb has to navigate CO's overcall + check-raise possibilities behind, where CO holds sets/two-pair/wraps disproportionately due to range-cap geometry. Raising as semi-bluff with AKo is dominated by raising T9s/JTs/QTs/K-high-FD candidates that have made-equity + redraws; AKo's blocker profile (blocks AQ/AJ which fold anyway, blocks KQ/AK which call) is poor for a raise. Calling realizes the gutshot at a discount, preserves position to bluff turn cards that brick CO (low non-spade non-heart non-T cards where MP gives up), and retains delayed-implied-odds on T turns where stacks go in vs flopped-two-pair. Equity-realization IP-closing is high (~0.90 multiplier) because hero closes action and sees a free river when checked to. RAISE mix exists at low frequency (~10-15%) as protection-and-fold-equity vs MP's weakest air on a board where checking back is unattractive, but pure GTO leans heavily toward CALL. FOLD is dominated — pot odds + nut-gutshot + overcard equity + position make folding strictly worse than calling. Verdict: CALL, ~88/12 mix.
